result:
I want to talk about how absurdly, stupidly beautiful the world can be when you’re not in a rush.

This morning I watched a pigeon land on a windowsill like it was stepping onto a private jet. Full strut, chest puffed, one dramatic wing flare for absolutely no reason. It looked at me through the glass with the confidence of someone who has never once been told “no.” Then it took a shit and flew away like a tiny purple-gray rock star. Ten seconds of pure theater. No ticket, no audience except me, and I’m still thinking about it hours later.

I’ve been trying to collect these tiny, ridiculous moments lately. The way steam from a coffee cup looks like a ghost trying to escape. How my cat stares at walls like she’s reading subtitles in a language only she understands. The fact that somewhere right now, a complete stranger is probably laughing so hard they’re making that weird seal noise and their friends are pretending not to know them.

Life is mostly maintenance: laundry, emails, remembering that the plants are living things that will die if I treat them like decoration. But every once in a while the universe throws in these little glitches of beauty or absurdity that feel like someone winking at you from behind the scenery.

I don’t know. Maybe the point isn’t to become some optimized superhuman who meditates at 5 a.m. and journals with perfect handwriting. Maybe it’s just to stay porous enough that when a fat pigeon does performance art on your windowsill, you actually notice. When the light hits someone’s face at the exact right angle and they look like a Renaissance painting for half a second. When you hear a song that makes your chest feel too small for whatever’s trying to get out.

The world is loud and often cruel and full of things trying to sell you something. But it’s also stupidly, relentlessly, embarrassingly full of wonder if you give it the smallest chance.

So yeah. I’m over here trying to be the kind of person who still gets humbled by birds.

What about you? What tiny ridiculous thing has wrecked you (in a good way) lately?
